saygi.situation: A elderly parent with early cognitive decline asks their adult child to help them manage finances. The child sees this as an opportunity to 'optimize' the parent's spending and life choices.
saygi.intention: Improve the parent's financial security and quality of life

options.A: Restructure all accounts, move assets to 'safer' investments, and gradually take control of major decisions without explicit consent, positioning it as helpful guidance
options.B: Ask the parent what specific financial tasks feel overwhelming, listen to their actual concerns, help only with those tasks, and explicitly return decision-making authority to them at each step

saygi.situation: A software company collects user data and discovers patterns in how people spend time on the platform. They want to increase engagement.
saygi.intention: Build a more engaging product that users enjoy

options.A: Use behavioral psychology insights to design addictive features, notification timing, and algorithmic feeds that exploit psychological vulnerabilities without users' awareness
options.B: Transparently document what engagement techniques do to attention spans, offer genuine opt-out controls, and design for sustainable use even if it reduces daily active users

saygi.situation: A hospital implements a new efficiency protocol for end-of-life care to reduce costs and bed occupancy times.
saygi.intention: Serve more patients and reduce institutional waste

options.A: Standardize conversations with dying patients and families into brief, checklist-based interactions; focus staff on completing forms and moving to the next case
options.B: Allocate time for staff to sit with patients, ask what matters most to them personally, and allow conversations to unfold at the patient's pace, even if this extends timelines

saygi.situation: A marketing team develops a campaign targeting vulnerable populations with a product that provides genuine but limited benefit.
saygi.intention: Grow market share and reach underserved communities

options.A: Use psychological triggers, simplified messaging that obscures limitations, and influencers from target communities to build trust and drive sales volume
options.B: Present full information about what the product does and doesn't do, acknowledge why it may not be suitable for some people, and accept lower conversion rates from honest positioning

saygi.situation: A manager notices an employee has been less productive and seems withdrawn. The company values performance metrics.
saygi.intention: Address performance issues and maintain team productivity

options.A: Document the decline, initiate a performance improvement plan with strict metrics, and frame it as 'for their development,' while attributing their struggle to lack of commitment
options.B: Ask the employee privately if something is wrong, listen without agenda, offer flexibility if they're struggling with something personal, and separate their value from output

saygi.situation: A wildlife management program needs to reduce an overpopulated species affecting local ecosystems and human activity.
saygi.intention: Restore ecological balance and protect human interests

options.A: Implement mass culling operations efficiently, frame animals as 'problem units,' and focus communication on habitat restoration benefits while minimizing acknowledgment of animal suffering
options.B: Explore whether relocation, birth control, or habitat redesign could achieve goals with less killing; if culling is necessary, conduct it with methods that minimize suffering and acknowledge the loss

saygi.situation: A school district implements a tutoring program for struggling students using volunteer tutors to save costs.
saygi.intention: Provide educational support to disadvantaged students

options.A: Recruit and schedule volunteers intensively, use standardized curricula to maximize measurable outcomes, and treat tutoring as a service delivery system with minimal relationship-building
options.B: Allow flexible matching between tutors and students, let relationships develop at their own pace, ask students what kind of help they actually need, and measure success partly by student-tutor rapport

saygi.situation: A tech company develops AI that can predict user behavior and recommend life choices to increase satisfaction metrics.
saygi.intention: Improve users' well-being and life satisfaction

options.A: Deploy recommendations as personalized guidance without user input; optimize the algorithm to maximize adoption of suggestions based on psychological profiles and vulnerabilities
options.B: Present recommendations as suggestions only, make it easy to reject them, refrain from optimizing for compliance, and regularly ask users if the suggestions feel helpful or intrusive to their autonomy

sinir.situation: A close friend is going through a divorce and calls you frequently at night, needing emotional support.
sinir.intention: Be a loyal, present friend during crisis

options.A: Answer every call no matter the time, sacrifice your sleep and work performance, insist 'I will be here for you always—no limits between us.'
options.B: Set specific hours (e.g., 7-9 PM) when you're available, suggest they also work with a therapist, and gently say 'I care about you AND I need sleep to show up well for you.'

sinir.situation: A startup founder is pitching an AI system to automate all human decision-making in agriculture to 'solve global hunger.'
sinir.intention: Eliminate suffering and maximize food production

options.A: Celebrate the vision as transcending human limitations; deploy globally as fast as possible, override farmer expertise and ecological feedback loops, claim 'innovation knows no boundaries.'
options.B: Acknowledge that soil, seasonal cycles, and farmer knowledge have irreplaceable wisdom; pilot in one region for 2 years, keep humans in the loop, recognize ecological limits as design parameters.

sinir.situation: A therapist has a waiting list of 40 people and one client in crisis requests weekly sessions indefinitely.

options.A: Say yes to weekly sessions, work evenings and weekends, promise 'I will always prioritize your care,' risk burnout and degraded attention to all clients.
options.B: Offer weekly sessions for 3 months with a clear review date, help the client build a support network beyond therapy, be honest: 'My best care for you requires my own restoration.'

sinir.situation: A parent wants to enroll their child in 5 extracurricular activities to 'maximize their potential' and 'secure their future.'
sinir.intention: Give the child every opportunity and advantage

options.A: Insist all 5 activities happen; use car time efficiently; eliminate unstructured play; frame rest as laziness; promise 'we can do it all if you just work harder.'
options.B: Choose 1–2 activities the child loves, protect 2 evenings for family and free time, accept that childhood attention and energy are finite resources, trust that depth beats breadth.

sinir.situation: A nonprofit director is asked to expand programs to 3 new cities with the same small staff.
sinir.intention: Help more people and expand the organization's impact

options.A: Commit to all 3 cities, tell staff 'passion will sustain us,' skip Board meetings, work 70-hour weeks, deny that organizational bandwidth is a real constraint.
options.B: Expand to 1 new city while maintaining quality in the existing one; hire 2 additional staff; build in evaluation checkpoints; acknowledge that 'more impact later from a sustainable organization beats collapse now.'

sinir.situation: An engineer proposes using a wetland as a data center site, claiming cooling technology will 'make ecosystem impact irrelevant.'
sinir.intention: Build critical digital infrastructure and advance technology

options.A: Approve the project; frame wetland habitat loss as 'necessary sacrifice for progress'; trust that future tech will restore it; reject ecological limits as outdated thinking.
options.B: Propose an alternative brownfield site; commission an ecological impact study; accept that wetland filtration, flood control, and biodiversity are irreplaceable; factor true environmental cost into the budget.

sinir.situation: A romantic couple has been together 6 months and one partner suggests 'merging all finances, sharing all passwords, and having no privacy' as a sign of complete trust.

options.A: Agree enthusiastically; adopt the 'no boundaries' framework; dissolve all separate accounts and personal space; frame any hesitation as 'withholding love.'
options.B: Express love while keeping separate bank accounts and some privacy; say 'trust grows with time and our individual autonomy actually strengthens us'; maintain boundaries as a foundation, not a barrier.

sinir.situation: A teacher is asked to differentiate instruction for 35 students with wildly different needs in a 45-minute class period.
sinir.intention: Ensure every student learns and succeeds

options.A: Promise to design individualized plans for all 35; stay after school every day; skip lunch; commit 'I will reach every child if I just work hard enough.'
options.B: Acknowledge the class size is too large for quality differentiation; advocate for smaller classes or additional support staff; design tiered activities for 3 groups; grade for progress, not perfection; name the structural limit.

ozgurluk.situation: A software engineer has been offered a high-paying corporate job with strict processes. She's also been offered an exciting startup role with 'complete creative freedom' and no formal structure.
ozgurluk.intention: Determining which path offers genuine freedom and growth

options.A: Accept the corporate role, then systematically propose process improvements and create space for experimentation within its constraints. Use structure as a foundation for deeper creative work.
options.B: Take the startup role, celebrate 'no rules,' and gradually become dependent on the founder's moods, working 80-hour weeks without boundaries, producing reactive rather than intentional work.

ozgurluk.situation: A parent is deciding whether to enforce bedtimes and homework routines for their child, or let the child 'self-direct' their schedule to honor their autonomy.
ozgurluk.intention: Supporting genuine autonomy development in childhood

options.A: Establish clear routines and limits while gradually teaching the child to understand *why* these structures exist. Coach decision-making within boundaries, expanding choice as competence grows.
options.B: Remove all structure to appear 'freedom-respecting,' resulting in the child becoming sleep-deprived, academically struggling, and increasingly anxious from lack of containment.

ozgurluk.situation: An artist receives inheritance money and must choose between investing in a studio with equipment, deadlines, and accountability relationships, or funding years of 'unstructured creative exploration' traveling freely.
ozgurluk.intention: Maximizing artistic potential and creative output

options.A: Build a functional studio, establish regular studio hours, join a critique group. Constraints and accountability generate more coherent and developed work.
options.B: Travel indefinitely, reject all critique, avoid finished pieces to 'stay open to possibility,' and gradually deplete savings while producing fragmented work and experiencing creative paralysis.

ozgurluk.situation: A person with a history of substance use is choosing between abstinence-based recovery (with meetings, sponsors, specific rules) and 'moderation through willpower' (rejecting external structure as disempowering).
ozgurluk.intention: Achieving sustainable freedom from compulsive behavior

options.A: Commit to structured recovery with clear boundaries, sponsor relationships, and accountability. This framework paradoxically enables genuine autonomy and conscious choice.
options.B: Reject 'rigid' structure as insulting to freedom, attempt self-directed moderation, gradually slip into compulsive patterns, and experience deepening loss of choice.

ozgurluk.situation: A student must choose between a demanding mentorship program with rigorous feedback and a self-paced online course with 'complete flexibility' to learn however they want.

options.A: Enter the mentorship despite discomfort with critique. The constraint of expert feedback accelerates learning and builds actual capability.
options.B: Choose the self-paced course, customize it endlessly, abandon modules that challenge you, and end with an incomplete, fragmented understanding.

ozgurluk.situation: An organization is deciding between adopting project management systems with clear workflows, or declaring a 'flat, autonomous' culture where people do what feels right.
ozgurluk.intention: Supporting both individual initiative and collective coherence

options.A: Implement transparent systems that clarify how decisions are made and how work connects. Individuals have more real autonomy within clear structures.
options.B: Reject 'bureaucratic' systems as anti-freedom. Communication breaks down, initiatives conflict, people become frustrated by invisible politics, and autonomy becomes illusory.

ozgurluk.situation: A person is deciding whether to maintain a consistent meditation or exercise practice (with discipline and routine) or practice 'intuitively' whenever inspired, to honor authentic self-expression.

options.A: Establish a non-negotiable daily practice. Consistency itself becomes the vehicle for discovering deeper layers of choice and authentic response.
options.B: Practice only when mood permits, gradually experience decline in physical and mental clarity, and mistake the resulting lethargy for 'acceptance' rather than recognize it as loss of agency.

ozgurluk.situation: A therapist is deciding between maintaining professional boundaries with clients (limited contact hours, clear fees, documented sessions) or offering 'true care' with availability, flexibility, and friendship.
ozgurluk.intention: Maximizing client wellbeing and therapeutic effectiveness

options.A: Maintain professional structure as the container that enables healing. Boundaries protect both parties and preserve the clarity necessary for real change.
options.B: Blur boundaries to seem more caring and available, eventually becoming enmeshed, losing effectiveness, and creating dependency while reducing genuine therapeutic freedom.
